title: Reconstructing the evolutionary origin of beta-catenin recognition in the Wnt destruction complex.
authors: Sun, Hongyan; Walters, Brian M; Zidek, Radim; Martindale, Mark Q; Wikramanayake, Athula H
one_liner_zh: 该文结合AlphaFold3结构预测与功能实验，研究Wnt破坏复合物中Axin与beta-catenin蛋白-DNA/蛋白互作的进化起源，虽非TF-DNA体系，但AI结构预测方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作建模。
abstract: Emergence of Wnt/beta-catenin signaling was a major metazoan innovation, yet how its core molecular interactions evolved remains unresolved. Here, we investigated evolution of the Wnt/beta-catenin destruction complex (BDC), a conserved regulatory module that represses Wnt/beta-catenin signaling by targeting cytoplasmic beta-catenin for degradation. In bilaterians, BDC activity depends on interactions between Axin, adenomatous polyposis coli (APC), and beta-catenin. However, bioinformatic analyses suggested that early-diverging metazoans lack the canonical beta-catenin-binding motifs required for these interactions raising questions about the origin of BDC function. Using functional assays in Nematostella vectensis, a representative of the Cnidaria, the outgroup to bilaterians, we demonstrate that both NvAxin and NvAPC regulate Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, indicating the presence of a BDC despite the lack of canonical bilaterian binding motifs. In vitro experiments revealed that NvAxin binds Nvbeta-catenin through previously unrecognized low-affinity interactions. Guided by AlphaFold3 predictions, we identified two beta-catenin-binding motif-like sequences in cnidarian Axin including one within the Axin-RGS domain, and a single motif in the Axin-RGS domain of placozoans, sponges, and ctenophores. Functional analyses showed that a conserved residue within these motifs is required for Axin-beta-catenin interaction. Our results support a model where an ancestral beta-catenin-binding motif-like sequence in Axin-RGS acquired weak beta-catenin-binding capacity in early-emerging metazoans followed by motif duplication in the cnidarian-bilaterian last common ancestor. In bilaterians, the duplicated beta-catenin-binding motif evolved higher affinity for beta-catenin, while the ancestral sequence was lost. By integrating phylogenetics, AI-based structural prediction, and experimental validation, we have revealed for the first time the molecular steps underlying functional evolution of a complex signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: Wnt/β-catenin信号通路的出现是后生动物的一项重大创新，然而其核心分子相互作用如何演化仍悬而未决。在此，我们研究了Wnt/β-catenin降解复合体（BDC）的演化，这是一个保守的调控模块，通过靶向细胞质中的β-catenin进行降解来抑制Wnt/β-catenin信号通路。在两侧对称动物中，BDC活性依赖于Axin、腺瘤性结肠息肉病蛋白（APC）和β-catenin之间的相互作用。然而，生物信息学分析表明，早期分化后生动物缺乏这些相互作用所需的典型β-catenin结合基序，这引发了关于BDC功能起源的问题。利用Nematostella vectensis（刺胞动物门的代表，两侧对称动物的外群）中的功能实验，我们证明NvAxin和NvAPC均调控Wnt/β-catenin信号通路，表明尽管缺乏典型的两侧对称动物结合基序，BDC仍然存在。体外实验揭示，NvAxin通过先前未被识别的低亲和力相互作用结合Nvβ-catenin。在AlphaFold3预测的指导下，我们在刺胞动物Axin中鉴定出两个β-catenin结合基序样序列，其中一个位于Axin-RGS结构域内，并在扁盘动物、海绵动物和栉水母的Axin-RGS结构域中鉴定出一个单一基序。功能分析表明，这些基序内的一个保守残基是Axin-β-catenin相互作用所必需的。我们的结果支持一个模型，即Axin-RGS中的祖先β-catenin结合基序样序列在早期出现的后生动物中获得了弱β-catenin结合能力，随后在刺胞动物-两侧对称动物最后共同祖先中发生基序重复。在两侧对称动物中，重复的β-catenin结合基序演化出对β-catenin更高的亲和力，而祖先序列则丢失。通过整合系统发育学、基于AI的结构预测和实验验证，我们首次揭示了复杂信号通路功能演化背后的分子步骤。
